A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with PAWS-VMK corresponding to MoLAR-SS in v4. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-classification and OOD-detection experiments, including component ablations, transfer experiments, and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds supervised MoLAR experiments and frozen-backbone CIDER/PALM evaluations, including detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: v4 adds fully supervised MoLAR alongside the semi-supervised method, introducing training with known labels and a cross-entropy branch in Figure 2 and Algorithm 3. MoLAR-SS otherwise retains PAWS-VMK's frozen backbone, averaged-and-sharpened targets, vMF-SNE initialization, and SKMPS selection.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven classification datasets and the same CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 OpenOOD dataset pairs. The added supervision and reference-bank configurations change procedures within existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The exemplar-based comparison in v4 Table 2 includes supervised MoLAR and CIDER/PALM alongside PAWS and the backbone. v3's corresponding frozen-backbone comparisons in Tables S6-S7 contained PAWS, PAWS-VMK, and the backbone, while CIDER/PALM appeared separately as ResNet comparisons. SSL comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: v4 adds fully supervised training, full-training-set versus exemplar-only OOD reference banks, and frozen-DINOv2 CIDER/PALM experiments with 70 training epochs against MoLAR's 50 plus 20 initialization epochs. Table 2 also states common SKMPS exemplars although its PAWS scores match v3's random-stratified results; a rerun is not established. Existing SSL splits and budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 extends the initialization/selection ablation to supervised MoLAR in Table 6 and tests whether reducing the OOD reference bank preserves detection performance. Existing SSL, convergence, diversity, transfer, RoPAWS, and hyperparameter analyses remain. The sharpening-versus-class-probability analysis in v3 Figure S6 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-run means and standard deviations for SSL, twenty-run diversity analyses with minimum/maximum error bars, and five-run defaults versus single-run alternatives in the hyperparameter study. The added OOD tables continue reporting point estimates without new uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: v4 Tables 1-2 and S9-S12 add substantial supervised and frozen-backbone OOD results. For example, supervised MoLAR reports CIFAR-100 near/far AUROC of 95.5/96.9 with the full reference bank and 95.9/97.0 with exemplars. These are newly evaluated conditions; the earlier SSL and semi-supervised OOD scores are retained under the MoLAR-SS name.

T1.justification: Most mixture-model, Bayes, and vMF-SNE mathematics is retained or relocated. However, v4 omits v3 Appendix A's explicit equal-prototype-count assumption from the classification derivation and adds the supervised objective in Equation 6. That equation averages probabilities, making its stated equivalence to cross-entropy incorrect.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from a PAWS-based SSL method with OOD capability to a unified supervised/semi-supervised OOD framework. v4 emphasizes OOD detection costing no more than classification, adds a first-of-its-kind semi-supervised OOD claim, and replaces the earlier state-of-the-art SSL framing with competitive SSL performance.

C2.justification: The DeepWeeds discussion now attributes poor initial separation to the randomly initialized projection head, whereas v3 described the corresponding panels as backbone embeddings. v4 also extends the efficiency interpretation to supervised MoLAR and reference-bank comparisons. The pretraining-overlap caveat already appeared in v3 Appendix C.

D1.justification: v4 adds an authors' code link, training pseudocode in Algorithm 3, and implementation provenance and training budgets for CIDER/PALM. However, it removes v3 Appendix F's extensive specifications for optimizers, learning-rate schedules, augmentations, batch sizes, projection-head architecture, and RoPAWS settings. This is a substantial documentation change, without establishing changes to those retained experiments.

R1.justification: v4 substantially repositions the work as an exemplar-based alternative to CIDER/PALM and asserts a new semi-supervised OOD novelty claim. It adds Lee et al.'s 2018 OOD work and removes references including SwAV, knowledge distillation, and several vMF/background works, while retaining the principal empirical comparator families.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and methodology are extensively rewritten around OOD detection. Terminology changes from prototypes/PAWS-VMK to exemplars/MoLAR, OOD results precede SSL results, the probabilistic derivation moves into the main text, and the appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. v4 adds a radar-chart overview, redraws and separates the training/initialization diagrams, adds supervised OOD tables, simplifies existing tables, and relocates retained plots. The sharpening plot and detailed hyperparameter tables are removed.

improvement.justification: The same-backbone CIDER/PALM comparisons and reference-bank experiments materially strengthen the OOD evidence beyond v3's comparisons across different backbones. However, v4 removes extensive replication settings and introduces an incorrect supervised-loss equivalence in Equation 6. The added code link does not resolve those issues within the supplied material. These empirical gains and losses in formal clarity and reproducibility leave the net overall quality change uncertain.
